title: Context Habitats — sprint diary (long-context heuristics)
content:
Quick framing (why I care)
- Running into tail user flows where prefix reuse is high but model quality drops with naive caching/eviction. Want small set of heuristics that are cheap to compute at request time and improve served quality for cached prefixes.
- Need something that can slot into Redwood serving runtime (low overhead, stateless per-request) and then test in Dedicated pool.

Papers skimmed & one-line takeaways
- "The Case for Conditional KV Compression" (arXiv 2305.x) — suggests compressing KV only when cache hit rate is low and sequences share low mutual information. Practical but needs good MI proxy.
- "Sparse Prefix Indexing for Long Context" — index prefixes by sparse hashing to find semantically-similar cached segments; promising but index maintenance expensive in streaming workloads.
- "Chunked Retrieval + Stitching" (NeurIPS short paper) — stitch model outputs across chunks with light re-ranking; reduces degeneracy but latency tradeoffs.

My running notes (observational)
- Observed pattern: conversational agents with repeated references to a handful of entities (product names, dates) generate heavy cache reuse; but when user switches topic the cached KV causes stale continuations.
- Useful signal: recent-turn novelty (token-level entropy delta) — if entropy drops after including cached prefix, that may indicate over-conditioning.
- Another cheap proxy: overlap ratio between last N tokens of incoming prompt and cached prefix start (character/byte n-gram overlap). Combined with a global approx similarity score gives a quick accept/reject.

Heuristic sketch (fast, stateless)
1) compute overlap_ratio = 3-gram overlap between prompt suffix (last 128 tokens) and cached prefix head (first 256 tokens)
2) compute quick_sim = hashed-similarity on sentence-embedding-lite (64d projection from a small embedder, quantized) — run in ~0.5ms on CPU
3) compute novelty_delta = estimated token-entropy(prompt) - estimated token-entropy(prompt + prefix) (approx by unigram log-prob from cached freq table)
4) decision rule: if (overlap_ratio < 0.05 and quick_sim < 0.45) OR novelty_delta < -0.3 => bypass cache (i.e., treat as cold)
- Rationale: low literal overlap + low semantic sim => likely different topic; also if adding prefix lowers entropy a lot (over-conditioning) then bypass.

Questions / uncertainties
- How noisy is the unigram freq entropy proxy in real queries? Need to sample logs and compute correlation with model perplexity change.
- Cost: small embedder on CPU might add P99 overhead. Could we reuse existing prod features (user_id, route metadata) to short-circuit?
- Interaction with batching: bypassing cache increases token compute; need to ensure not thrash autoscaler. Tie decision to current node load or model-cost budget.

Quick experiment plan (3-stage)
A) Offline sim (cheap) — replay 10k requests from prod logs with recorded KV hits, compute heuristics and approximate "delta-quality" using log-prob and a 1-gram BLEU to previous ground-truth. Measure FPR/FNR relative to naive cache accept-all.
B) Canary: integrate heuristic into Dedicated test pool with 5% traffic, track latency, cost-per-token, and a lightweight user-facing quality metric (top-1 token agreement with full-run). Flag regressions.
C) Metrics & rollout gating — require: no >1% drop in top-1 agreement, <2% increase in P99 latency, overall token-cost delta < +3% for canary. If positive quality lift with acceptable cost, scale to 25%.

Notes on implementation specifics (runtime constraints)
- Implement quick_sim as a stored 64-bit locality-sensitive hash (LSH) per cached prefix for constant-time comparisons. When cache entries created, precompute LSH.
- Overlap_ratio computed with rolling fixed-size Bloom filters of last 8k tokens, stored in metadata — small memory.
- novelty_delta uses small rolling unigram table updated per session; or approximate via reservoir-sampled global counts to avoid per-session state.

Action items (next 2 weeks)
- [ ] Pull 30k anonymized prompt+cache pairs from past 60 days (ask Data Eng for export) — due 2026-09-20. See linked artifact (GitHub issue #87) for sample schema.
- [ ] Write offline sim harness (python) to compute overlap_ratio, quick_sim (use tiny-embedder mimic), and novelty_delta. Target: run in <1h on local laptop for 30k items. Owner: me. Due: 2026-09-22.
- [ ] Proto integration PR for runtime LSH metadata and accept/bypass flag (minimal change to request path) — pair with runtime engineer. Ask @Hannah for review. Due: 2026-09-29.

Slack links and cross-references (internal)
- Basic design discussion thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0ABCDEF/p1690001112000000 (see messages on Sept 10–14)
- Related infra ticket: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/issues/87

Loose ideas for later (parking lot)
- Adaptive thresholds per-route: model usage and user population may need different thresholds (support A/B + per-route config).
- Learning a tiny scorer: collect human preferences on 3k samples and train a 2-3k param MLP to predict whether to use cache; requires label pipeline.
- Consider eviction policies informed by semantic clustering of prefixes, not just LRU.

Final quick note to self
- Keep the offline sim as close to prod as possible: include tokenization differences, streaming prefix shapes, and exception handling (e.g., code blocks). If offline sim shows promising precision/recall for bypass decisions, it should be safe to canary.

References clipped (for later reading)
- Conditional KV compression — arXiv:2305.14147 (skim)
- Sparse Prefix Indexing — group repo link (TODO fetch)
- Chunked Retrieval + Stitching — NeurIPS short paper (2025)

End of sprint scratch — will iterate after offline sim results.
